note: "King's Chamber Southern Shaft 2.49 m". The findings page, ADDITIONAL MEASUREMENTS, SHAFT INLETS WITHIN THE CHAMBERS, read on 2026-09-16 from the isida-project.org mirror named on this source. Gantenbrink measures "the distance between the east wall of the chambers and the east wall of the shafts", and the scene lays the bore's centre line on this offset, so the drawn shaft stands about half a shaft-width, a tenth of a metre, east of where its centre truly is. That is stated rather than corrected, because correcting it would mean storing a sum of two records instead of the figure the survey published. This replaces an estimate of 5.24 m, which was the middle of the chamber wall, entered because the record it replaced said "Gantenbrink’s inlet positions are on his drawing and not in his text". They are in his text, on the findings page rather than on the four shaft pages, which is where the earlier reading stopped. The southern shaft of the King’s Chamber moves 2.75 m east by this, and its computed outlet on the face moves with it onto the 5.20 m east of the axis that the same page measures for it.
Height of the channel's floor above the chamber floor at the south wall. The Edgars (1910, §497) crept into it holding a candle, so it is low in the wall; no source in hand gives the figure.

8.35 and 8.65 in at the top, §56, the S. channel's width where it could be reached from the outer end; stored as the mean, 8.5 in. Petrie adds that it is not straight in the clear length, curving more than its own width to the east, which the straight legs here do not follow.
8.7 to 8.9 in, §56, the S. channel's height; stored as the mean, 8.8 in, square to the floor.
“This initial horizontal shaft segment is 1.72 meters long”, the upper southern shaft page: the run through the granite wall block before the shaft turns up.
Horizontal: the same sentence of the upper southern shaft page.
The run at the first angle is one block, Gantenbrink's Block No. 2, whose length is on his drawing and not in his text; a course block of the core is a metre and a half or so. Sigma is half of that.
“At the beginning of Block No. 2 the shaft inclines at an angle of 39.20° (manually measured)”, the upper southern shaft page.
The steeper run holds “to the end of Block No. 4”, two blocks, whose lengths are on Gantenbrink's drawing; two course blocks. Sigma is half of that.
“At Block No. 3 the shaft inclines more sharply, reaching an angle of 50.54° (manually measured), which it maintains to the end of Block No. 4”, the upper southern shaft page.

The last leg runs until it meets the south face, where Petrie found the mouth: §33 has the S. channel coming out in the 104th course. Under Goyon's course table the leg comes out at about 80.6 m, the top of his 104th course, which is Petrie's 103rd or 104th; the two counts differ by two courses over the whole pyramid.

“From this point, all the way to the outlet on the pyramid's flank (we measured both points), the shaft maintains an angle of 45°”, the upper southern shaft page, from Block No. 5 on. Petrie's theodolite means over the outer 840 in run 44°26′ to 45°30′ with a mean of 45°13′40″, §56. The same figure as kc.shaft.south.angle, which claim C2 compares to Alnitak.

Height of the channel's floor above the chamber floor at the north wall; no source in hand gives the figure.
8.9 to 9.2 in, mean 9.0, §56, the width of the original N. channel where its floor and west side survive in the forced working passage.
8.72 and 8.74 in, §56; stored as the mean, square to the floor.
“The lower end of the shaft begins with a 2.63 meter horizontal section through the first block”, the upper northern shaft page.
Horizontal: the same sentence of the upper northern shaft page.

The bent run from Block No. 2 to the beginning of Block No. 5, which Caviglia's 1817 tunnel follows and Gantenbrink measured onto his drawing: “At Block No. 2 the shaft angles upward and simultaneously bends to the West.” Three blocks, drawn here as one leg of three course blocks. Sigma is half of that.
The bent run's slope is on Gantenbrink's drawing only; the straight run above it is at 32.60°, so the same figure is used here with a sigma wide enough for the bends.

Azimuth of the bent run: north with a lean to the west, which is the direction Gantenbrink's text gives and the Grand Gallery to the east is the reason for. The amount is on his drawing only. Twenty degrees west of north over the leg's length is a westward shift of about a metre and a half; sigma covers half that again.

The last leg runs until it meets the north face, where Petrie found the mouth: §33 has the N. channel coming out in the 103rd course. Under Goyon's table the leg comes out at about 80.8 m, his 105th course, which is Petrie's 103rd within the two-course difference between the counts.

“The angle between this point and the point of the shaft's outlet on the flank of the pyramid (we measured both points) is 32.60°”, the upper northern shaft page, from Block No. 6 on; the outer 11 m through the plunderers' tunnel average 31.20° by hand, and Petrie's means over the outer 372 in are 30°43′ to 32°05′, §56. The same figure as kc.shaft.north.angle, which claim C2 compares to Thuban.

Height of the channel's floor above the chamber floor at the south wall; no source in hand gives the figure.
“about 8 wide”, §44, said of the N. channel and taken for both; Gantenbrink calls the shafts about 20 by 20 cm.
8.8 in high in the chamber wall, §44.

“After an initial horizontal section of 1.96 meters (penetrating the first block of the Queen's Chamber wall), the shaft inclines”, the lower southern shaft page. Petrie has the horizontal part at 80.0 in, §44, which is 2.03 m.
Horizontal: the same sentence of the lower southern shaft page.

The sloping run up to the blocking slab: the 1993 campaign diary for March 22nd has Upuaut-2 reach the slab “at 59 meters”, measured along the shaft from its mouth in the chamber, less the 1.96 m horizontal run. The shaft continues past the slab, as the 2002 and 2011 robots found; nothing beyond it is drawn.

“the shaft inclines at an average angle of 39.6078°, which we determined by taking 24 measurements over a distance of 28 meters”, the lower southern shaft page. Petrie's goniometer at the chamber end gives 38°28′, §44. The same figure as qc.shaft.south.angle, which claim C2 compares to Sirius.

Height of the channel's floor above the chamber floor at the north wall; no source in hand gives the figure.
“about 8 wide in the chamber wall”, §44.
8.6 in high, §44.

“After an initial horizontal section of 1.93 meters (penetrating the first block of the Queen's Chamber wall), the shaft bends upwards”, the lower northern shaft page. Petrie has it at 76 in, §44, which is 1.93 m.
Horizontal: the same sentence of the lower northern shaft page.

The run up to the bend: the 1993 diary has Upuaut-2 reach “a sharp bend at 18 meters” along the shaft from its mouth, and the lower northern shaft page puts the turn at the end of Block No. 9, after the 17 m over which the angle was measured; 18 m less the 1.93 m horizontal run.

The figure qc.shaft.north.angle carries, so the drawn shaft and claim C2's ray agree. Gantenbrink's 1999 page says the angle of ascent “fluctuates between 33.3° and 40.1°” over 14 measurements in the first 17 m, with a deliberate change at Block No. 4, and Petrie's goniometer at the chamber end gives 37°28′, §44; sigma spans that.

The westward dog-leg that carries the shaft clear of the Grand Gallery: “At the end of Block No. 9, the shaft angles about 45° to the West, in order to avoid the static structure of the Great Gallery.” How far it runs before turning back north was mapped by the 2002 Pyramid Rover and is not in a source in hand; the Gallery is 2.1 m wide and stands east of the passage axis, so a leg of this length on that bearing shifts the shaft about 5.7 m west of it. Sigma is half the leg.
The dog-leg is assumed to keep the shaft's slope; nothing in hand says it changed.
“angles about 45° to the West”, the lower northern shaft page: north-west, azimuth 315°.

The run back on the northern bearing to the blocking stone the 2002 Pyramid Rover found, reported at about the same distance up the shaft as the southern shaft's slab; 64 m in all less the two legs below. No source in hand gives the figure. Nothing beyond the stone is drawn.
The slope is assumed to continue; see qc.shaft.north.segment.2.angle.

"King's Chamber Southern Shaft ... Shaft width 18 cm". The findings page, ADDITIONAL MEASUREMENTS, SHAFT INLETS WITHIN THE CHAMBERS, read on 2026-09-16 from the isida-project.org mirror named on this source. This is the section at the inlet itself, which is not the section Petrie gives on the same shaft: his is where he could reach it, and the report notes that "in the vicinity of the chambers and the sharply-angled shaft segments, the fluctuations are larger", shaft width running 17 to 22 cm and height 14 to 23.5 cm against averages of 20.5 and 21.5 cm. Kept under its own key rather than on <shaft>.width so that the two are not conflated; nothing is built from it yet.
